title: The Typewriter of Vilna
premise: In 1918, Juniper Hartwell, indentured to the Baltic Trading Company in Vilna, recognizes the handwriting on a smuggled letter as that of her father — declared dead five years ago when his pearl boat sank. The letters, typed on a distinctive typewriter, are being used to forge armistice documents that could save or doom hundreds of refugees competing for the last evacuation berths. As Juniper traces the typewriter through occupied Vilna's black markets, she discovers her father alive but coerced by occupying officers, and must decide whether exposing him saves her found family of dockworkers and refugees or condemns them. In the end, she forges one final page herself — trading her father's freedom for the berth that carries her chosen family to safety, while she stays behind to sign the armistice witness roll under a name that is finally, truly hers.
about_author: Jude Eastwick is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing displaced-persons records across the Baltics before turning to fiction. They write about people history filed away, and live between Riga and a houseboat on the Daugava.

chapters.title: Salt in the Ledger
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Working the Vilna counting-house, Juniper catalogs cargo and silences, hiding her literacy from the company clerk who owns her contract. A crate of salvaged pearl-boat wreckage arrives bearing a water-stained ledger in her father's hand. The beat: grief reopened, the first crack in five careful years.

chapters.title: The Stranger at Pier Nine
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. A scarred stranger named Tomas asks pointed questions about the wrecked boat Perla and pays in German marks too new to be honest. He claims the ledger is evidence in an arms inquiry; Juniper lies about having seen it. Beat: fear sharpening into curiosity — she keeps the ledger.

chapters.title: What the Dead Write
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Tomas reveals he was the Perla's navigator, that the sinking was staged to smuggle pearls past the blockade, and that the captain — Juniper's father Elias — survived. He shows a typed note he swears is Elias's, though it came off a machine, not a pen. Beat: hope arriving like contraband.

chapters.title: The House of Borrowed Names
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper brings the ledger to the tenement family that raised her since indenture: Mirele the seamstress, her sons Dov and Anshel, and old Frau Zemel. Reading Elias's entries aloud, they realize the 'pearls' were coded names of smuggled refugees. Beat: found family becomes co-conspirators.

chapters.title: Typewriter Nº 7
chapters.summary: Dov's POV. Dov, a repair-shop apprentice, identifies the typing as coming from a rare Adler model sold to the occupation administration — meaning Elias writes under military supervision. They trace three surviving machines in Vilna. Beat: the enemy has a serial number.

chapters.title: Silences That Keep People Safe
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The company clerk suspects Juniper's night movements and threatens to sell her contract south. She bargains with stolen information instead, buying weeks. Flashback to her mother teaching her which silences protect. Beat: duty versus love made personal.

chapters.title: Letters to No Address
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Tomas intercepts a courier carrying typed pages to Berlin and finds lists of refugee names — some marked for berths, others for detention. One list includes everyone in Mirele's tenement. Beat: the stakes turn from mystery to mortal.

chapters.title: The Berth List
chapters.summary: Mirele's POV. The tenement learns the last neutral ship, the Aldona, leaves before the armistice with room for eleven. Eleven neighbors, thirty-one souls. Mirele, who lost children to earlier pogroms, begins quietly deciding whom to push forward. Beat: love curdling into impossible arithmetic.

chapters.title: A Room Above the Print Shop
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Following the Adler trail, Juniper rents a room above a print shop where a clerk types occupation documents nightly. Through the floorboards she hears two voices — one of them her father's, older, broken, unmistakable. Beat: reunion deferred by terror.

chapters.title: Elias Hartwell, Deceased
chapters.summary: Elias's POV (first time). Elias explains how he survived the staged wreck, was blackmailed into forging documents, and typed the ledger pages hoping someone would read the code. He believes Juniper drowned with her mother. He does not know she lives upstairs. Beat: dramatic irony as heartbreak.

chapters.title: Ink Under the Floorboards
chapters.summary: Anshel's POV. Young Anshel tails the print-shop clerk and is nearly caught; Juniper pulls him out, blowing her cover to the occupation officer Captain Vogel, who now knows her face. Beat: the cost of family — protection requires exposure.

chapters.title: Vogel's Offer
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Vogel offers Juniper a devil's trade: her father's release and one guaranteed berth in exchange for the original ledger, which proves the smuggling network. She pretends to consider. Beat: temptation with her father's voice inside it.

chapters.title: What Mirele Decided
chapters.summary: Mirele's POV. Mirele has ranked the tenement by need and secretly put her own name last. Dov discovers the list and confronts her; she says a mother's arithmetic is not negotiable. Beat: the theme of sacrifice made explicit and contested.

chapters.title: The Forger's Hand
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Ordered to type a final document — a version of the armistice terms altered to void civilian evacuations — Elias inserts deliberate errors, buying days. Vogel grows suspicious. Beat: quiet sabotage, rising dread.

chapters.title: Night of the Long Ledgers
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper breaks into the print shop to copy the true armistice text, meets her father face to face for the first time in five years. Thirty seconds of embrace before alarms. Beat: climax of longing — reunion interrupted.

chapters.title: Betrayal, Priced
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Tomas, revealed to be feeding information to both sides to save his own brother, sells the tenement's escape plan to Vogel. Two neighbors are detained. Beat: betrayal from within the found family; trust shatters.

chapters.title: Eleven Berths, Twelve Names
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. With the Aldona departing in forty-eight hours, Juniper holds all the pieces: the ledger, the true armistice text, Vogel's offer, and Dov's knowledge of typewriters. She proposes forgery — a berth authorization typed on Adler Nº 7. Beat: decision crystallizes.

chapters.title: The Last Page
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Father and daughter type the forged authorization together, four hands on one machine, his errors corrected by her memory of his hand. To authenticate it, Elias must surrender himself to Vogel. Beat: climax — love against duty resolved in ink.

chapters.title: Armistice
chapters.summary: Multiple brief POVs. The real armistice is signed; bells, gunfire, confusion. Elias trades himself for the tenement's passage; Vogel, outmaneuvered, can only watch the Aldona load. Beat: catharsis amid chaos.

chapters.title: The Aldona Departs
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. On the pier, Mirele tries to give Juniper her own place aboard. Juniper refuses — she has signed the witness roll under her full name and will stay to testify for her father and the detained. Beat: choosing family over safety, freely.

chapters.title: Which Silences Keep People Safe
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV, months later. Juniper testifies at the inquiry, secures Elias's release, and reclaims her indenture papers. The tenement letters arrive from abroad like heartbeats. Beat: resolution — silence transformed into testimony.

chapters.title: Nº 7, Retired
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV, epilogue. Juniper buys Adler Nº 7 at auction and sets it in Mirele's empty workshop, typing the first page of the tenement's true history. Final line echoes her mother: some silences keep people safe; this one won't. Beat: memory preserved, story handed to the reader.
